investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T00:48–00:56Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and the expected-output contract (check-expectations.json line 256–259) receives an empty evidence object, failing all four required fields. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource pool exhausted: all existing remote-agent VMs are occupied and no capacity remains on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing any new pod from being scheduled. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were removed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk. No source evidence of a config change is present; sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty.

Tertiary — kata-containers or peer-pods daemonset degraded on the 2 eligible nodes: the nodes may be present and labeled correctly but the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertiser (device plugin or peer-pods operator) may have stopped reporting capacity, causing the scheduler to see 0 available slots even if physical capacity exists.

Quaternary — eval probe token or org resolution failure causing createAgent to be called with an invalid orgId: less likely because the scheduler error is explicit and appears before any API-level failure, and requireOrgId is called before createAgent in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1884).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T00:48–00:56Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and the expected-output contract (check-expectations.json line 256–259) receives an empty evidence object, failing all four required fields. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unscheduled for 136s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty {}; all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent creation call never returned a result.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: contract gap lists orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState as entirely missing.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod unscheduled for 143s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause affects the state check.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod unscheduled for 147s, empty evidenceKeys — same root cause affects the runtime check.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required:true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs=143109 is within the outage window but the check failed on scheduling, not latency.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource pool exhausted: all existing remote-agent VMs are occupied and no capacity remains on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing any new pod from being scheduled. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were removed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk. No source evidence of a config change is present; sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty.

Tertiary — kata-containers or peer-pods daemonset degraded on the 2 eligible nodes: the nodes may be present and labeled correctly but the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertiser (device plugin or peer-pods operator) may have stopped reporting capacity, causing the scheduler to see 0 available slots even if physical capacity exists.

Quaternary — eval probe token or org resolution failure causing createAgent to be called with an invalid orgId: less likely because the scheduler error is explicit and appears before any API-level failure, and requireOrgId is called before createAgent in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1884).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval probe was stuck Unschedulable for 136–147 seconds before the check timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the state of the production-api Kubernetes cluster at the time of the run.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes, which are then fully saturated.

Tertiary — insufficient cluster autoscaling or peer-pod quota: the cluster may lack autoscaling for kata-capable nodes, or the upstream peer-pod provider quota is exhausted, preventing new VM-capable nodes from joining.
Lower probability — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, which could self-resolve if workloads complete.
